# WEA Fishing Port Landings {#wind_port}

**Description**: Port Landings from within Wind Lease Areas and Community Social Vulnerability Indicators

**Found in**: State of the Ecosystem - Gulf of Maine & Georges Bank (2022+), State of the Ecosystem - Mid-Atlantic (2022+)

**Indicator category**: Database pull with analysis

**Contributor(s)**: Angela Silva, Doug Christel
  
**Data steward**: Angela Silva
  
**Point of contact**: Angela Silva <angela.silva@noaa.gov>
  
**Public availability statement**: Source data are NOT publicly available. Please email angela.silva@noaa.gov for further information and queries of Speed and Extent of Offshore Wind Development indicator source data.

## Methodology Summary

This indicator compute the fishing port landings and associated revenue originating from federally designated Wind Energy Area (WEA) lease areas and links these values to the community level social vulnerability indicators. To evaluate the relative significance of WEA-based landings for coastal communities, fishing activity is spatially linked to wind lease areas and aggregated at the port level.

Three spatial definitions are used to evaluate the data: 
(1) wind lease areas that are under construction or completed, 
(2) wind lease areas not yet under construction, and
(3) all wind lease areas combined. 
Multiple datasets are used to support the indicator which also includes non-confidential port level revenue data for reporting, species port level data for contextual interpretation and total port revenue data for normalization.

All revenue values are converted to constant 2024 USD using the GDP deflator which insures the comparability across years. Community Social Vulnerability Indicators are joined to port level results to provide additional context for interpreting potential socioeconomic exposure associated with offshore wind development.

## Methods
### Data sources
Social Indicators Data: 
*https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/national/socioeconomics/social-indicators-coastal-communities
*https://www.st.nmfs.noaa.gov/data-and-tools/social-indicators/

Wind Data: 
*https://www.greateratlantic.fisheries.noaa.gov/ro/fso/reports/WIND/ALL_WEA_BY_AREA_DATA.html
*https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/resource/data/socioeconomic-impacts-atlantic-offshore-wind-development


### Data analysis

Cumulative port landings(pounds) and revenue(dollars) from Wind Energy Areas (WEA) were pulled for communities along the Northeast US Shelf from 2010 to 2019. Percent of wind lease area landings were calculated compared to total landings for those communities. Social Vulnerability indicators were then matched to these communities. 


### Data processing 

Data were formatted for inclusion in the `ecodata` R package using the R code found [here](https://github.com/NOAA-EDAB/ecodata/blob/master/data-raw/get_wind_port.R).

## Data Limitations and Assumptions

When interpreting this indicator, a number of limitations should be taken into account. The lack of publicly available source data for estimating fishing activity within wind lease areas restricts the analysis's ability to be independently reproduced. Therefore, rather than exact attribution, the results are meant for contextual and comparative interpretation.

The indicator excludes ports with less than five years of data and/or average annual revenue from wind lease areas of less than $10,000, which could skew the results in favor of larger or more consistently active ports. Additionally, years with no reported wind lease revenue are not included, which could understate variability for ports with sporadic activity.

Fisheries management council designations, which are regarded as static over time and might not accurately reflect changes in management jurisdiction or regulatory structure during the analysis period, are the basis for species-level analyses. Applied at the community level, social vulnerability indicators should be understood as contextual data rather than as the primary causes of observed fishing patterns.
